mn27:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.
mn27:2.1: Now on that occasion Jānussoni of the divine caste drove in broad day through Sāvatthī in a chariot drawn by mares, all in white.
mn27:2.2: He saw the wanderer Pilotika coming.
mn27:2.3: When he saw him, he asked him:
mn27:2.4: ‘Now where is Master Vacchāyana coming from in broad day?’
mn27:2.5: ‘Sir, I am coming from the monk Gotama’s presence.’
mn27:2.6: ‘How does Master Vacchāyana conceive the monk Gotama’s ability of understanding? He is wise, is he not?’
mn27:2.7: ‘Sir, who am I to know the monk Gotama’s ability of understanding.
mn27:2.8: One would surely have to be his equal to know the monk Gotama’s ability of understanding.’
mn27:2.9: ‘Master Vacchāyana praises the monk Gotama with high praise indeed.’
mn27:2.10: ‘Sir, who am I to praise the monk Gotama,
mn27:2.11: the monk Gotama is praised by the praised—as best among gods and men.’
mn27:2.12: ‘What value does Master Vacchāyana see that he has such confidence in the monk Gotama?’
mn27:3.1: ‘Sir, suppose a wise elephant-woodsman went into an elephant wood,
mn27:3.2: and he saw in the elephant wood a big elephant’s footprint long in extent and broad across,
mn27:3.4: “It is a bull elephant and a big one.”
mn27:3.5: So too, as soon as I saw four footprints in the monk Gotama, I concluded:
mn27:3.6: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”
mn27:4.2: ‘Sir, I have seen here certain warrior-noble caste scholars that were clever and knew others’ theories as a hairsplitter (marksman knows archery): one would fancy they must go about demolishing views with the understanding that they have.
mn27:4.4: “The monk Gotama will visit such a village or town.”
mn27:4.6: “We shall approach the monk Gotama and ask him this question.
mn27:4.7: If he is asked like this, he will answer like this, and so we shall prove his theory wrong;
mn27:4.8: and if he is asked like this, he will answer like this, and so again we shall prove his theory wrong.”
mn27:4.10: “The monk Gotama has come to visit such and such a village or town.”
mn27:4.11: They go to the monk Gotama.
mn27:4.12: The monk Gotama instructs, urges, rouses and encourages them with a talk on the Dhamma.
mn27:4.13: After that they do not so much as ask him the question, so how should they prove his theory wrong?
mn27:4.14: In actual fact they become his disciples.
mn27:4.15: When I saw this first footprint in the monk Gotama, I concluded:
mn27:4.16: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered on the good way.”
mn27:5.1: ‘Again, I have seen certain divine caste scholars that were clever … this second footprint … the Sangha has entered on the good way.”
mn27:6.1: ‘Again, I have seen certain householder scholars that were clever … this third footprint …
mn27:6.2: the Sangha has entered on the good way.”
mn27:7.1: ‘Again, I have seen certain monk scholars that were clever and knew others’ theories as a hair-splitter (marksman knows archery): one would fancy they must go about demolishing views with the understanding that they have.
mn27:7.3: “The monk Gotama will visit such and such a village or town.”
mn27:7.5: “If he is asked like this, he will answer like this, and so we shall prove his theory wrong,
mn27:7.6: and if he is asked like this, he will answer like this, and so again we shall prove his theory wrong.”
mn27:7.7: They hear: “The monk Gotama has come to visit such and such a village or town.”
mn27:7.8: They go to the monk Gotama.
mn27:7.9: The monk Gotama instructs, urges, rouses and encourages them with talk on the Dhamma.
mn27:7.10: They do not so much as ask him the question, so how should they prove his theory wrong?
mn27:7.11: In actual fact they ask the monk Gotama to allow them to go forth from the home life into homelessness,
mn27:7.12: and he gives them the Going-forth.
mn27:7.13: Not long after they have gone forth in this way, dwelling alone and withdrawn, diligent, ardent and self-controlled, by realization themselves, with direct knowledge they here and now enter upon and abide in that supreme goal of the life divine for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn27:7.15: “We were very nearly lost, we were very nearly undone,
mn27:7.16: for formerly we claimed that we were monks though we were not, we claimed that we were divines though we were not, we claimed that we were Arahants though we were not,
mn27:7.17: but now we are monks, now we are divines, now we are Arahants.”
mn27:7.18: When I saw this fourth footprint in the monk Gotama, I concluded:
mn27:7.19: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, the Sangha has entered on the good way.”
mn27:7.20: ‘As soon as I saw these four footprints in the monk Gotama I concluded:
mn27:7.21: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered on the good way.” ‘
mn27:8.1: When this was said, Jānussoni of the divine caste got down from his chariot drawn by mares, all in white, and arranging his robes on one shoulder, he raised his hands palms together towards where the Blessed One was, and uttered this exclamation three times:
mn27:8.2: ‘Honour to the Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened!
mn27:8.3: Honour to the Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened!
mn27:8.4: Honour to the Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened!
mn27:8.5: Now suppose that, sometime or other, we were to meet Master Gotama and have some conversation with him?’
mn27:9.1: Then Jānussoni of the divine caste went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him,
mn27:9.2: and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.
mn27:9.3: When he had done so, he related to the Blessed One all his conversation with the wanderer Pilotikā.
mn27:9.4: When this was said, the Blessed One told him:
mn27:9.5: ‘At this point, divine, the simile of the elephant’s footprint has not yet been completed in detail.
mn27:9.6: So listen then how it is completed in detail
mn27:9.7: and attend carefully to what I shall say.’
mn27:9.8: ‘Yes, sir,’ Jannussoni of the divine caste replied.
mn27:10.1: ‘Divine, suppose an elephant woodsman went into an elephant wood,
mn27:10.2: and he saw in the elephant wood a big elephant’s footprint long in extent and broad across:
mn27:10.3: a wise elephant woodsman would not yet conclude
mn27:10.4: “It is a bull elephant and a big one.”
mn27:10.6: In an elephant wood there are small cow elephants that leave a big footprint. It might be the footprint of one of those.
mn27:10.8: As he does so, he sees in the elephant wood a big elephant’s footprint long in extent and broad across and something used high up:
mn27:10.9: a wise elephant woodsman would not yet conclude
mn27:10.10: “It is a bull elephant and a big one.”
mn27:10.12: In an elephant wood there are tall cow elephants with prominent teeth that leave a big footprint. It might be the footprint of one of those.
mn27:10.14: As he does so, he sees in the elephant wood an elephant’s footprint long in extent and broad across and something used high up and marks made by tusks:
mn27:10.15: a wise elephant woodsman would not yet conclude
mn27:10.16: “It is a bull elephant and a big one.”
mn27:10.18: In an elephant wood there are tall cow elephants with tusks that have a big footprint. It might be the footprint of one of those.
mn27:10.20: As he does so, he sees in the elephant wood an elephant’s footprint long in extent and broad across and something used high up and marks made by tusks and broken-off branches.
mn27:10.21: And he sees the bull elephant at the root of a tree or in the open, walking about or standing, sitting or lying down.
mn27:11.1: ‘So too, divine, here a Tathāgata appears in the world, Arahat and Fully Enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.
mn27:11.2: ‘He declares this world with its gods, its Māras and its (Brahmā) Divinities, this generation with its monks and divines, with its kings, and men, which he has himself realized by direct knowledge.
mn27:11.3: ‘He teaches Dhamma good in the beginning, good in the middle and good in the end, with (the right) meaning and phrasing, and he announces a life divine that is utterly perfect and pure.
mn27:12.1: ‘A householder or householder’s son or one born in some clan hears that Dhamma.
mn27:12.2: On hearing the Dhamma he acquires faith in the Tathāgata.
mn27:12.3: Possessing that faith, he considers thus:
mn27:12.4: “House life is crowded and dirty; life gone forth is wide open.
mn27:12.5: It is not possible, living in a household, to lead a life divine as utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell.
mn27:12.6: Suppose I shaved off hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness?”
mn27:12.7: ‘And on another occasion, abandoning perhaps a small, perhaps a large fortune, abandoning perhaps a small, perhaps a large circle of relatives, he shaves off hair and beard, puts on the yellow cloth, and goes forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn27:13.1: ‘Being thus gone forth and possessing the bhikkhus’ training and way of life, abandoning killing living beings, he becomes one who abstains from killing living beings, with rod and weapon laid aside, gentle and kindly, he abides compassionate to all beings.
mn27:13.2: ‘Abandoning taking what is not given, he becomes one who abstains from taking what is not given, taking (only) what is given, expecting (only) what is given, he abides pure in himself by not stealing.
mn27:13.3: ‘Abandoning what is not the life divine, he becomes one who lives the life divine, who lives apart abstaining from vulgar lechery.
mn27:13.4: ‘Abandoning false speech, he becomes one who abstains from false speech, he speaks truth, cleaves to truth, is trustworthy, reliable and undeceiving of the world.
mn27:13.5: ‘Abandoning malicious speech, he becomes one who abstains from malicious speech: as one who is neither a repeater elsewhere of what is heard here for the purpose of causing division from these, nor a repeater to these of what is heard elsewhere for the purpose of causing division from those, who is thus a reuniter of the divided, a promoter of friendships, and enjoying concord, rejoicing in concord, delighting in concord, he becomes a speaker of words that promote concord.
mn27:13.6: ‘Abandoning harsh speech, he becomes one who abstains from harsh speech: he becomes a speaker of such words as are innocent, pleasing to the ear and lovable, as go to the heart, are civil, desired of many, and dear to many.
mn27:13.7: ‘Abandoning gossip, he becomes one who abstains from gossip: as one who tells in season what is true and beneficial and the Dhamma and Discipline, he becomes a speaker of timely words, worth recalling, reasoned, measured and connected with good.
mn27:13.8: ‘He becomes one who abstains from injuring seeds and plants.
mn27:13.9: ‘He becomes one who eats in only one part of the day, refusing (food) at night and late meals.
mn27:13.10: ‘He becomes one who abstains from dancing, singing, music and theatrical shows.
mn27:13.11: ‘He becomes one who abstains from wearing of garlands, smartening with scent and embellishment with unguents.
mn27:13.12: ‘He becomes one who abstains from high and large couches.
mn27:13.13: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting gold and silver.
mn27:13.14: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting raw corn.
mn27:13.15: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting raw meat.
mn27:13.16: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting women and girls.
mn27:13.17: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting bondswomen and bondsmen.
mn27:13.18: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting sheep and goats.
mn27:13.19: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting poultry and pigs.
mn27:13.20: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting elephants, cattle, horses and mares.
mn27:13.21: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting fields and lands.
mn27:13.22: ‘He becomes one who abstains from going on errands.
mn27:13.23: ‘He becomes one who abstains from buying and selling.
mn27:13.24: ‘He becomes one who abstains from false weights, false metal and false measures.
mn27:13.25: ‘He becomes one who abstains from cheating, deceiving, defrauding and trickery.
mn27:13.26: ‘He becomes one who abstains from wounding, murdering, binding, brigandage, plunder and violence.
mn27:14.1: ‘He becomes one who is content with robes to keep the body, with alms-food to keep the belly: wherever he goes he takes all with him.
mn27:14.2: Just as wherever a winged bird flies it flies using its own wings,
mn27:14.3: so too he becomes one who is content with robes to keep the body, with alms-food to keep the belly: wherever he goes he takes all with him.
mn27:14.4: ‘Possessing this store of Noble Ones’ virtue, he feels in himself pleasure that is blameless.
mn27:15.1: ‘He becomes one who, on seeing a visible form with the eye, apprehends no signs and features
mn27:15.2: through which, if he left the eye faculty unguarded, evil unprofitable dhammas of covetousness and grief might invade him. He practises the way of restraint, he guards the eye faculty, undertakes the restraint of the eye faculty.
mn27:15.3: On hearing a sound with the ear …
mn27:15.4: On smelling an odour with the nose …
mn27:15.5: On tasting a flavour with the tongue …
mn27:15.6: On touching a tangible with the body …
mn27:15.7: On cognizing a dhamma with the mind he apprehends no signs and features
mn27:15.8: through which, if he left the mind faculty unguarded, evil unprofitable dhammas of covetousness and grief might invade him. He practises the way of restraint, he guards the mind faculty, undertakes the restraint of the mind faculty.
mn27:15.9: ‘Possessing this Noble Ones’ faculty restraint, he feels in himself pleasure that is blameless.
mn27:16.1: ‘He becomes one who acts in full awareness when moving forward and moving backward, who acts in full awareness when looking towards and looking away, who acts in full awareness when flexing and extending, who acts in full awareness when wearing the patched cloak, robes and bowl, who acts in full awareness when eating, drinking, chewing and tasting, who acts in full awareness when evacuating the bowels and making water, who acts in full awareness when walking, standing, sitting, waking up, talking and keeping silent.
mn27:17.1: ‘Possessing this store of the Noble Ones’ virtue, and possessing this Noble Ones’ faculty restraint, and possessing this Noble Ones’ mindfulness and full awareness,
mn27:17.2: he resorts to a secluded resting-place—to the forest, a tree-root, a rock, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a woodland solitude, an open space, a heap of straw.
mn27:18.1: ‘On return from his alms-round after the meal, he sits down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, establishing mindfulness before him.
mn27:18.2: ‘Abandoning covetousness for the world, he abides with a mind free from covetousness, he purifies mind from covetousness.
mn27:18.3: Abandoning ill-will and hatred, he abides without a mind of ill-will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings, he purifies mind from ill-will and hatred.
mn27:18.4: Abandoning lethargy and drowsiness, he abides with a mind free from lethargy and drowsiness, percipient of light, mindful and fully aware, he purifies mind from lethargy and drowsiness.
mn27:18.5: Abandoning agitation and worry, he abides unagitated with a mind stilled in himself, he purifies mind from agitation and worry.
mn27:18.6: Abandoning uncertainty, he abides with a mind crossed beyond uncertainty, unquestioning about profitable dhammas, he purifies mind from uncertainty.
mn27:19.1: ‘Having thus abandoned these five hindrances, imperfections of mind that weaken understanding,
mn27:19.2: quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unprofitable dhammas, he enters upon and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained application, with happiness and (bodily) pleasure born of seclusion.
mn27:19.3: ‘This is called a footprint of a Tathāgata, something used by a Tathāgata, something marked by a Tathāgata,
mn27:19.4: but a noble disciple does not yet conclude:
mn27:19.5: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”’
mn27:20.1: ‘Again, with the stilling of initial and sustained application, he enters upon and abides in the second jhāna, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without initial application and without sustained application, with happiness and pleasure born of concentration.’
mn27:20.2: ‘This also is called a footprint of a Tathāgata …’
mn27:20.3: the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”’
mn27:21.1: ‘Again, with the fading as well of happiness he abides in equanimity, mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, he enters upon and abides in the third jhāna on account of which Noble Ones announce: “He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.”’
mn27:21.2: ‘This also is called a footprint of a Tathāgata …’
mn27:21.3: the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”’
mn27:22.1: ‘Again, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, he enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.’
mn27:22.2: ‘This also is called a footprint of a Tathāgata, something used by a Tathāgata, something marked by a Tathāgata,
mn27:22.3: but a noble disciple does not yet conclude:
mn27:22.4: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”’
mn27:23.1: ‘When the concentrated mind is thus purified and bright, unblemished, rid of defilement and become malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs, he inclines the mind to knowledge of recollection of past life …
mn27:23.2: (as in Sutta 4, para. 27)… thus with its aspects and particulars he recollects his manifold past life.’
mn27:23.3: ‘This also is called a footprint of a Tathāgata, something used by a Tathāgata, something marked by a Tathāgata,
mn27:23.4: but a noble disciple does not yet conclude:
mn27:23.5: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”’
mn27:24.1: ‘When concentrated mind is thus purified … and attained to imperturbability, he directs, he inclines the mind to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings …
mn27:24.2: (as in Sutta 4, para. 29)… thus with heavenly eyesight, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees … how beings pass on according to their kammas.’
mn27:24.3: ‘This also is called a footprint of a Tathāgata, something used by a Tathāgata, something marked by a Tathāgata,
mn27:24.4: but a noble disciple does not yet conclude:
mn27:24.5: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”
mn27:25.1: ‘When concentrated mind is thus purified … and attained to imperturbability, he directs, he inclines the mind to knowledge of the exhaustion of the taints.
mn27:25.2: He understands as it actually is: “This is suffering” … (complete as in Sutta 4, para. 31) …
mn27:25.3: He understands as it actually is: “This is the way leading to the cessation of taints.”
mn27:25.4: ‘This also is called a footprint of a Tathāgata, something used by a Tathāgata, something marked by a Tathāgata,
mn27:25.5: but a noble disciple has not already concluded, but rather is in the act of concluding:
mn27:25.6: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”
mn27:26.1: ‘Knowing thus, seeing thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, from the taint of being, and from the taint of ignorance.
mn27:26.2: When liberated, there is the knowledge “It is liberated”.
mn27:26.3: He understands: “Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived out, what can be done is done, there is no more of this to come.”
mn27:26.4: ‘This also is called a footprint of a Tathāgata, something used by a Tathāgata, something marked by a Tathāgata.
mn27:26.5: It is at this point that a noble disciple has concluded:
mn27:26.6: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered upon the good way.”
mn27:26.7: ‘It is at this point, divine, that the simile of the elephant’s footprint has been completed in detail.’
mn27:27.1: When this was said, Jāņussoni of the divine caste said:
mn27:27.3: The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama, as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, holding up a lamp in the darkness for those with eyesight to see forms.
mn27:27.4: ‘I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma and to the Sangha.
mn27:27.5: From today let Master Gotama remember me as a follower who has gone to him for refuge for life.’
